title: [Core] Use array to speedup padding (#6779)

experiments.name: make_tensor_with_pad
experiments.workload: SamplingTensors padding-input prep + 2x make_tensor_with_pad (prompt+output), input_len=1024, batch_size=2048, pad=vocab_size(32000), dtype=int64, device=cpu; 1 warmup, 5 timed repeats
experiments.note: FINDING: PR #6779 does NOT touch make_tensor_with_pad; that fn is BYTE-IDENTICAL at base and gold (already the np.full/make_ndarray_with_pad array path). The real change is the INPUT fed to it inside SamplingTensors.from_sampling_metadata/from_lists: base builds List[List[int]] via list(seq_data.prompt_token_ids) (tuple->list copies); gold passes seq_data.prompt_token_ids_array (array('l')) directly, SequenceData now storing tokens as array. Benchmark loads the REAL unmodified make_tensor_with_pad from each mounted tree by source (vllm import chain needs the absent _custom_ops C ext) and replicates the exact per-arm prep path. speedup_x = mean of per-run base/gold ratios.

environment: docker vllm-cpu-bench:21222 (CPU torch 2.15.0+cpu, numpy 2.5.4), colima arm64 Mac; identical image for both arms, only vllm/ source tree differs; real make_tensor_with_pad loaded by source from each mounted tree
